Basic operations on discrete time series

Source: R/dts.R
dts-operations.Rd

These functions implement standard operations on discrete time series represented by dts objects (see dts()), preserving their state space.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'dts'
x[i, ...]

# S3 method for class 'dts'
x[[i, ...]]

# S3 method for class 'dts'
length(x)

# S3 method for class 'dts'
rev(x)

Arguments

x

a dts object.

i

indices specifying the elements to extract.

...

not used.

Value

  • x[i] returns a dts object with the selected observations and the same state space as x (including the states that are absent from the selection);

  • x[[i]] returns the i-th observation, as a value of the state space (see states());

  • length(x) returns the number of observations of x;

  • rev(x) returns a dts object with the observations of x in reverse order and the same state space.

See also

dts(), dts_data(), states()

Examples

x <- dts(c("A", "B", "C", "A", "A"))
length(x)
#> [1] 5
x[[2]]
#> [1] "B"
## the state space is preserved
x_short <- x[1:2]
x_short
#> Discrete time series of length 2 with state space A, B, C
#>  A B
states(x_short)
#> [1] "A" "B" "C"
rev(x)
#> Discrete time series of length 5 with state space A, B, C
#>  A A C B A
